title: Singapore's Position on Russian-Ukraine War One Year On
what_it_is: Singapore's Position on Russian-Ukraine War One Year On

sections.label: Singapore position on Ukraine invasion
sections.summary: Singapore condemned Russia's attack on Ukraine as a gross violation of the UN Charter and international law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) whether remarks on the Russia-Ukraine war by the Minister for Home Affairs at a workshop on 8 March 2023 held at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute represent the views of the Government; and (b) whether there has been any revision to Singapore's position on the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have taken – and we must continue to take – a clear stand that is consistent with our principles and our national interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In the Ministerial Statement of 28 February 2022 on the "Situation in Ukraine and Its Implications", Singapore strongly condemned Russia’s attack on Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The invasion of a sovereign country is a gross violation of the principles of the UN Charter and of international law.

sections.label: Ministers' statements reflect Government
sections.summary: Under collective responsibility, Ministers' statements reflect the Government's views while it is in charge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Needless to say, under the principle of collective responsibility, you can take it that, as long as we are in charge, the statements of each Minister reflect the views of the Government.

sections.label: Opposition agrees Russia invasion wrong
sections.summary: The Opposition ensured politics stops at the border, agreeing Russia's invasion breached international law and the UN Charter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I am very glad that in fact, the Opposition, of all parties, has ensured that politics stops at the border.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think I can quite safely say that, on behalf of every single Member in this House, our position remains that it was wrong of Russia, it was a breach of international law and of the principles of the UN Charter for them to launch the invasion of Ukraine.

sections.label: Ukraine invasion wrong, people pay
sections.summary: Singapore's position is that the invasion is wrong, a breach of international law, and people pay the ultimate price.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Ukraine and Ukrainians are paying the ultimate price.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, our position is clear: that it is wrong, a breach of international law, a flagrant violation of the principles of the UN Charter, the primary victim is the smaller country and it is people who are paying the ultimate price.

sections.label: Might-is-right order threatens small states
sections.summary: A world order based on might is right is profoundly inimical to the security and survival of small states.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: A world order based on might is right or where the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must, such a world order is profoundly inimicable to the security and survival of small states.

sections.label: Speech cleared with Cabinet
sections.summary: The speech was cleared with the highest levels of the Cabinet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For the Member's understanding, I cleared the speech with the highest levels of the Cabinet.

sections.label: Small countries and superpower manoeuvres
sections.summary: The speaker says he does not wish words put into his mouth or public pronouncements beyond what he has said, warning small countries against being caught up in superpower manoeuvres and rhetoric.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And therefore, there may be times when what I say publicly is entirely aimed at achieving that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I do not wish to have words put into my mouth, or to make public pronouncements beyond what I have already said, to say that beware that small countries do not get caught up in the manoeuvres, the to-ing and fro-ing, and the dangerous, sometimes escalatory, rhetoric or action the superpowers engage in.

sections.label: Agreement with Government stand
sections.summary: The speaker says there is no reason to disagree with the Government's consistent stand from February last year to now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Yes, Sir, we have no reason to disagree with the Government's consistent stand from February last year to now.
